root_cause.text: Using devm_spi_register_controller() (which automatically unregisters the SPI controller via devm cleanup on device removal) alongside an explicit spi_unregister_controller() call in the remove() callback, leading to a double-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "The driver uses devm_spi_register_controller() for registration, which automatically unregisters the controller via devm cleanup when the device is removed. The manual call to spi_unregister_controller() in the remove() callback can lead to a double-free." The patch fixes this by switching to spi_register_controller() (non-devm) so that the manual unregistration is the only one.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the exact registration call using devm, which automatically unregisters the SPI controller on device removal. Combined with an explicit spi_unregister_controller() in the remove callback, this leads to a double-free of the controller structure.
This allocates DMA buffer pages in the probe function. When double-free occurs due to devm cleanup and explicit unregister, these pages are freed twice, causing a use-after-free or corruption.

This completes the allocation of DMA buffer pages. The buffer is a resource that is later double-freed when the device is removed, because both the devm cleanup and the explicit spi_unregister_controller() trigger its release.

This checks if the DMA buffer allocation failed. While not directly causing the double-free, it is part of the allocation path that creates the resource subject to double-free. The vulnerability also involves the failure path if registration fails later.

This checks the return value of devm_spi_register_controller(). In the error path, it may free resources, but if registration succeeds, the devm cleanup will still happen on removal. The double-free arises regardless of this check.

This jumps to error handling if registration fails. While it is part of the probe function, the double-free vulnerability occurs when registration succeeds and later removal triggers both devm cleanup and explicit unregister, making this error path irrelevant to the root cause.
